problem:
Let $[T]_{B}$ and $[T]_{C}$ be the matrices of a linear transformation $T$ relative to the bases $B$ and $C,$ respectively. If ${P}_{C\to B}$ is the change-of-coordinates matrix from basis $C$ to basis $B,$ which of the following statements are true?

- $[T]_{C}={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1}$
- $[T]_{C}={P}_{C\to B}^{-1}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}$
- $[T]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1}$
worked_solution:
The connection between the matrices of our linear transformation $T$ relative to the bases $B$ and $C$ is given by the following diagram:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14075067/assets/9ba3d1f0eebdfc82c40f36bdbe16896ca15516b623c695b72c331861955329bc.png)

Here, moving along an arrow means pre-multiplying by the corresponding matrix. Algebraically, we can write this as

$$
[T]_{C}={P}_{C\to B}^{-1}\cdot [T]_{B}\cdot {P}_{C\to B},
$$

where ${P}_{C\to B}$ is the change-of-coordinates matrix from $C$ to $B.$

Solving this equation for $[T]_{B},$ we obtain the alternative formulation

$$
[T]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}\cdot [T]_{C}\cdot {P}_{C\to B}^{-1}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
